source.title: Layer-wise Adaptive Step-Sizes for Stochastic First-Order Methods for Deep Learning

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification performance of adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers using a different experimental setup from the optimizer-generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The CNN experiments report validation classification accuracy for several optimizers. These results bear on V4; batch size is fixed and other claim versions are not tested. Learning-rate plots and sensitivity results are not separate claim-version rows.
record.test_reason: The standard AdamW versus momentum-SGD comparisons report held-out image-classification accuracy in three dataset/architecture settings and bear on V4. Learning rate and weight decay were tuned; this does not directly reproduce V4's learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the CNN conclusion: layer-wise variants have similar or sometimes better optimization and generalization performance than tuned SGD-m and AdamW without global learning-rate tuning. Weight decay still requires tuning, and the variants take roughly 1.8 times as much process time.
record.recipe_differences: Compares tuned SGD-m and AdamW, plus layer-wise variants; uses CNN image-classification datasets with data augmentation, weight decay, and validation-based hyperparameter search. It does not reproduce the optimizer-comparison studies' full benchmark settings.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR-10 + VGG16, update frequency T=25 makes SGD-m-LW unstable; AdamW-LW accuracy is reported as insensitive across T={5, 10, 15, 20, 25}.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed layer-wise variants achieve competitive CNN accuracy relative to their standard counterparts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature-based layer-wise learning rates can preserve or improve classifier accuracy while avoiding global learning-rate search.

fits_no_version.finding: Shampoo and KFAC achieve the reported CNN accuracies as second-order optimizer benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second-order optimization methods can achieve competitive image-classification accuracy under tuned recipes.

record.problems: Only three CNN dataset/model combinations are reported for held-out accuracy; each uses data augmentation and weight decay. The text reports no uncertainty estimates, and the experiments are not designed to measure train-test gaps directly.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant held-out accuracy rows from the three CNN problems were left out. Autoencoder results focus on training loss, while GCN results report training accuracy and are not rows for V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and local-connectivity interventions.

Learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning; language benchmarks; controlled expansion of tuning breadth; Adam versus AdamW; switching to SGD; and quantitative comparison of training performance at the reported held-out accuracies.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings and their association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 2 accuracy values are transcribed correctly. Subjects are optimizers applied to the named architectures, rather than model identities themselves. Results use batch size 512, augmentation, and weight decay. CIFAR test sets also serve as validation sets for selecting hyperparameters, so their reported accuracies are selection-dependent. Near ties qualify the setting-dependent claim; they do not challenge its probabilistic wording. The study does not isolate the benefit of decoupled weight decay because it includes no standard Adam comparator.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, limited-tuning comparisons, broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, and the stated word-level language-model exception.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation of large-batch training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring subsequent test accuracy.

rows.subject: SGD-m
rows.operation_detail: Trained with tuned learning rate and weight decay; accuracy reported for the CIFAR-10 + VGG16 problem.
rows.check: Valid comparison baseline, but SGD-m accuracy alone cannot establish an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. The CIFAR-10 test set was used for validation and hyperparameter selection.

rows.subject: AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Trained with tuned learning rate and weight decay; accuracy reported for the CIFAR-10 + VGG16 problem.
rows.note: AdamW accuracy is lower than SGD-m in this setting.
rows.check: AdamW is 1.40 percentage points below SGD-m, a clear disadvantage rather than a partial effect. Weight decay was tuned alongside learning rate.

rows.subject: SGD-m-LW
rows.operation_detail: Trained with layer-wise adaptive step sizes and tuned weight decay; accuracy reported for the CIFAR-10 + VGG16 problem.
rows.check: Reports performance of the study's proposed SGD-m-LW method; it does not isolate the standard adaptive-versus-SGD comparison or a broader-tuning intervention.

rows.subject: AdamW-LW
rows.operation_detail: Trained with layer-wise adaptive step sizes and tuned weight decay; accuracy reported for the CIFAR-10 + VGG16 problem.
rows.note: Layer-wise variant of AdamW; accuracy is close to SGD-m.
rows.check: Reports performance of the proposed AdamW-LW method. Changing the optimization algorithm does not directly test V4's tuning, decoupled-weight-decay, or switching qualifications.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 with batch-normalized VGG16; learning rate and weight decay tuned
relationships.reason: R2 reports AdamW accuracy of 92.26% versus 93.66% for SGD-m in R1, a 1.40-point disadvantage under this recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy is 92.26% for AdamW versus 93.66% for momentum SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18; learning rate and weight decay tuned
relationships.reason: R8 and R7 report essentially equal AdamW and SGD-m accuracies, 74.71% and 74.69%; no adaptive disadvantage is established in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly achieved nearly the same accuracy as momentum SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: SVHN with DenseNet-121; learning rate and weight decay tuned
relationships.reason: R14 and R13 report nearly equal AdamW and SGD-m accuracies, 95.81% and 95.85%, without uncertainty estimates.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracies were nearly equal, but the comparison remains unverified and uncertainty was unreported.
